conclusion: Manufacturer lists one optical S/PDIF input supporting 12–96 kHz and a 48 kHz DSP sampling rate for V TWELVE DSP MK2.
limitations: Only applies if installed DSP is the MK2 model. Does not establish that the installed unit is that exact model.
physicalVerification: Read the amplifier model/revision label; verify optical lock at 48 kHz on bench.

conclusion: DSP PC-Tool documents Main Routing for analog plus additional HEC/AUX and Digital In paths, with separate digital routing options.
limitations: The documentation describes routing paths; simultaneous mix, warning sound behavior, source detection and preset-specific interaction need actual configuration test.

conclusion: DIRECTOR supports source volume adjustment for Digital optical, from -60 dB to 0 dB in 0.5 dB steps; Input Select can select sources when configured.

physicalVerification: Confirm exact DSP/DIRECTOR compatibility, firmware and intended routing; test digital contribution mute while analog Tesla audio remains uninterrupted.

conclusion: Enhance Auto describes a Panda-compatible Wi-Fi interface at 192.168.4.1 using UDP port 1338 for third-party CAN applications.
limitations: The page does not provide a stable supported SDK contract or guarantee of production telemetry signal fields/frequency. It notes client connection constraints.

conclusion: Enhance Auto warns third-party app connections may pause Dash data or cause disconnects; reliable Pi streaming alongside current Dash is not established.
limitations: Vendor guidance may change with firmware and hardware generation; no independent concurrent telemetry client support guarantee found.

conclusion: Tesla service bulletin R3 includes 2024+ Model 3 third-party CAN interface details for certain builds and the X181 interface.
limitations: Applicability is production/market dependent; Tesla states third-party wiring is unsupported and at installer risk. Not permission to modify vehicle wiring.
physicalVerification: Verify exact vehicle applicability in current Tesla service docs and have a qualified installer identify supported access without public disclosure of VIN.

conclusion: Pi 4B offers a 1.8 GHz Cortex-A72 vs Pi 3B+ 1.4 GHz Cortex-A53 and retains a 40-pin header. Pi 4 is the preferred bench candidate for headroom.
limitations: No automotive environmental qualification; low-latency real-time performance depends on OS/audio stack and must be measured.
physicalVerification: Confirm available Pi exact model/RAM/revision and stress-test audio callback and underrun handling.

conclusion: HiFiBerry identifies Digi2 Pro 2.2 as compatible with newer 40-pin Pi models including Pi 4, with optical TOSLINK output and a datasheet covering 44.1–192 kHz (TOSLINK caveats apply).
limitations: Pi 4 Rev 1.5 compatibility caveat documented by manufacturer; exact output mode and optical rate to HELIX must be bench-tested. No price retained because current VAT-inclusive Dutch/EU landed price was not verified.

conclusion: Use deterministic procedural oscillator/noise/resonator synthesis driven by a smoothed virtual RPM/load model; keep DSP real-time path offline and bounded.
limitations: Engine Sim is a reference only; license, code portability, performance and sound quality are not yet assessed. No licensed production assets selected.
physicalVerification: Prototype synthetic telemetry input and measure callback execution time, underruns, clipping and response latency.

conclusion: Set <50 ms accelerator-to-audible response as a system acceptance target. Allocate measured budget to telemetry, processing, buffers, optical/DSP and acoustic output.
limitations: No component latency claims can yet guarantee this system target.
